capability: Hear a colour set as one chord
title: Let the colours ring.

hook.picture: Close on the whale sliding colour cards onto the line one at a time. Each new card is judged only against the one beside it, and the whale nods every time.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: I stared at these colours so long they all looked fine.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: designer at six, before the client call

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: three palettes in a row. Each time a new card is matched to its neighbour only, the far end slides further off (every 2 beats, then 1, then half).
why_it_keeps_happening.words: Eyes only compare a colour to its neighbour.

stakes.body: A page ships with colours that fight, and the client sees it before you do.

solution_hint: Hear the whole set at once.

metaphor.body: Each colour card sends up a ring. The rings stack into one chord above the line, so the whole set is heard at once instead of judged pair by pair.

steps.picture: The whale taps the cards. Each sends one ring up, and four rings stack into one chord shape above the line.
steps.sound: Four just-tuned voices enter one by one.

steps.picture: The whale slides one card lighter. Its ring climbs, and the whole chord shape changes with it.
steps.words: Change one colour. The chord changes too.
steps.sound: One voice rises, the chord re-voices.

steps.picture: Push-in: the whale swaps a card for a near-twin it cannot tell apart by eye. The chord shape shifts, and an English Red ring marks the change.
steps.words: Ears catch a change tired eyes miss.
steps.sound: The chord audibly shifts on the swap.

steps.picture: The whale plays the set twice. Two ring stacks land exactly on top of each other, and a tick lands.
steps.sound: Same chord twice, then a soft tick.

real_case.claim: The studio's Orpheum engine maps each of its 19 curated Wada palettes to a 4-voice just-intonation chord, deterministically (gate G24).

source.title: CETI Motion Atlas Studio Pro README (Orpheum/GEOME engine, gate G24)

honest_limit.picture: A pale-on-pale colour set plays a calm, sweet chord, yet the pod's page in those colours is unreadable. The chord never noticed.
honest_limit.words: A sweet chord can still be unreadable.

not_this.body: Sound is a second sense, not a judge.

ending_pattern.body: The whale adds one more colour as in FELT, hears the chord shift, checks the page and swaps the card before sending. The pod answers ✓.
ending_pattern.callback: Same close shot as bar 1, the one-more-colour gesture, now caught by ear before it ships.

end_belief.body: Before you ship colours, listen to them.

beats.picture: Close: the whale slides a fourth colour card onto the line, glances at the card beside it, nods.
beats.sound: One soft pluck per card, slightly detuned.

beats.picture: A pod renders a page in those colours. Its text turns muddy against the ground, and the pod answers with an English Red ✕ chip.
beats.words: It looked fine until it shipped.

beats.picture: The whale adds a fifth card next to the fourth. The pair looks fine, and the page gets muddier.
The whale squints at the pod's ✕, blinks. Hold.
beats.camera: Close z 1.7, hold on the whale's face

beats.picture: Half a bar of stillness, then the title.
beats.camera: Still z 1.6, half bar of stillness

beats.picture: Pull back: three past colour rows. In each, every card matches its neighbour, but the first and last cards clash.
beats.words: Eyes only compare a colour to its neighbour.
beats.sound: Problem motif once: a chord with one voice a quarter-tone flat.

beats.picture: Three more cards drop in, every 2 beats, then 1, then half. Each one is matched only to its neighbour, and the far end drifts further.
Motion stops. A faint ring ghosts above every card at once.
beats.words: Hear the whole set at once.

beats.picture: Wide: nineteen short lines, each with its row of cards. Each plays its chord and earns a tick, nineteen ticks in a row.

beats.picture: The whale replays one row. The two chords overlap exactly, and the tick does not move.
beats.words: Same colours give the same chord, always.

beats.picture: A pale-on-pale colour set plays a calm, sweet chord. A pod renders a page in it and the words vanish. The pod answers ✕.
beats.words: A sweet chord can still be unreadable.
beats.sound: Signature chord plays once and does not resolve.

beats.picture: Slow push to the faded words on the pod's page.
beats.camera: One slow push to the thing that slipped

beats.picture: FELT framing: the whale reaches for one more card. Its ring shifts the chord. The whale stops, checks the page, and swaps the card.
beats.camera: Close z 1.6, the FELT framing restored

beats.picture: The pod renders the page: crisp text and a ✓ chip. The four rings glow and the whale sparks.
The settled card row, the rings fading, the whale breathing.
beats.words: Before you ship colours, listen to them.

score_self.reason: The problem is very relatable and the hint is plain. Risk: viewers may read the chord as a beauty judge, so the limit has to land hard. The case card is self-reported. No jargon is named, which keeps it clean.
